questions.q: What did Yahweh command Moses to tell the Israelites about the land of Canaan?
questions.a: He commanded Moses to tell them that when they entered Canaan, they would receive it as their own land within specific borders.

questions.q: What places marked the southern border of the land?
questions.a: The southern border went from the wilderness of Zin, near Edom, to the Salt Sea, then west past Kadesh Barnea to the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.q: What was the western border of the land?
questions.a: The western border was the Great Sea, that is, the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.q: What places marked the northern border of the land?
questions.a: The northern border went from the Great Sea to Mount Hor, then to Lebo Hamath, Zedad, and Ziphron, ending at Hazar Enan.

questions.q: What places marked the eastern border of the land?
questions.a: The eastern border went from Hazar Enan to Shepham, then to Riblah, along the east side of the Sea of Chinnereth, and down the Jordan River to the Salt Sea.

questions.q: Who were the people who would receive the land of Canaan as their possession?
questions.a: The nine and one half tribes of Israel would receive the land of Canaan as their possession.

questions.q: What would the descendants of Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh receive as their share of the land?
questions.a: The descendants of Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh would receive their share of land from across the Jordan at Jericho eastward.

questions.q: Who were the men who would divide the land for their inheritance?
questions.a: The men would be Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and one leader from every tribe.

questions.q: What did Yahweh command these men to do?
questions.a: He commanded them to divide the land of Canaan and to give each tribe of Israel its share.

commentary.text: The bounds of the promised land.
Those appointed to divide the land.

Verses 1–15 Canaan was of small extent; as it is here bounded, it is but about 160 miles in length, and about 50 in breadth; yet this was the country promised to the father of the faithful, and the possession of the seed of Israel. This was that little spot of ground, in which alone, for many ages, God was known. This was the vineyard of the Lord, the garden enclosed; but as it is with gardens and vineyards, the narrowness of the space was made up by the fruitfulness of the soil. Though the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof, yet few know him, and serve him; but those few are happy, because fruitful to God. Also, see how little a share of the world God gives to his own people. Those who have their portion in heaven, have reason to be content with a small pittance of this earth. Yet a little that a righteous man has, having it from the love of God, and with his blessing, is far better and more comfortable than the riches of many wicked. (Nu 34:16-29)

God here appoints men to divide the land to them. So sure must they feel of victory and success while God fought for them, that the persons are named who should be intrusted with the dividing of the land.
